advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `main` fail (or warn loudly) when zero SKILL.md files are discovered under the default root.
evidence: scripts/check_skill_frontmatter.py:156-171: `checked = 0` ... loop over `files` ... `if total_problems: ... return 1` else `print(f"PASS: {checked} ..."); return 0`
ABSENCE: no assertion that at least one SKILL.md was found before returning 0
advisory.finding: `main` returns 0 (prints 'PASS: 0 SKILL.md file(s)') when no SKILL.md files are discovered, so the gate silently no-ops if examples/agent-skills is renamed/moved or emptied — defeating the purpose of a gate meant to catch silently-dropped skills.
scenarios: examples/agent-skills is renamed or its SKILL.md files removed
the checker is invoked with a stale/incorrect default root after a directory reorg
advisory.suggested_fix: When `roots` is the DEFAULT_ROOT and `files` is empty, print an error and return a non-zero exit so an accidental relocation of the skills tree reddens CI instead of vacuously passing.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Error out when an explicitly-passed path argument does not exist rather than silently matching nothing.
evidence: ABSENCE: no `root.exists()` check; a non-existent Path silently yields no matches
advisory.finding: A nonexistent or mistyped path argument is silently treated as 'no problems': `find_skill_files` calls `root.is_file()` (False) then `root.glob('**/SKILL.md')` (empty) with no error, so `python check_skill_frontmatter.py bogus/path` exits 0.
scenarios: operator passes a wrong path to the CLI and assumes the clean exit means their file passed
advisory.suggested_fix: In `find_skill_files`, raise or record an error when `root` was explicitly supplied but does not exist (e.g. `if not root.exists(): ...`).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that runs main([...,'--github']) (or calls _emit_github) and asserts a `::error file=...,title=skill-frontmatter::` annotation is emitted, including the % / CR / LF escaping.
evidence: ABSENCE: no test in tests/unit/test_check_skill_frontmatter.py passes '--github' or asserts on a `::error file=...` annotation string; the only main() calls are `chk.main([])`, `chk.main([str(p)])`, `chk.main([str(tmp_path)])`.
advisory.finding: The --github annotation output path is entirely untested. Neither main() with --github nor _emit_github() is exercised, so a regression in the ::error:: annotation format or in the %/CR/LF escaping (a documented feature and CI-facing behavior) would not be caught.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test using capsys: write a bad skill, call `chk.main([str(p), '--github'])`, and assert the captured stdout contains a line starting with `::error file=` and that a description containing '%'/newlines is escaped to `%25`/`%0A`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a boundary test with multi-byte characters (e.g. 1024 multi-byte chars passes, 1025 fails) to lock in the character-count (not byte-count) semantics the docstring claims.
evidence: scripts/check_skill_frontmatter.py:20 `Lengths are counted in characters, not bytes, matching the spec.`
ABSENCE: no test uses a multi-byte character (e.g. an emoji or accented char) near the cap boundary to distinguish character-count from byte-count.
advisory.finding: The documented character-vs-byte length semantics for the description/name caps are unguarded. The docstring states 'Lengths are counted in characters, not bytes,' but every boundary test uses single-byte ASCII, so a regression to len(desc.encode()) would still pass at exactly 1024/64.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test where description is 1024 multi-byte characters (whose UTF-8 byte length exceeds 1024) and assert check_file returns [], plus a 1025-char variant that fails.
